title: 4B Setup
teaches: The 4B- (Stan Weinstein) as we trade it: after a Stage 4 decline under a falling 30-week line, a stock that has seen its low for the cycle sets a higher low on drying volume, reclaims the 50-day and pauses above it with room to run, the buy is the trade through the pause high at market once price is back above the 200-day and never more than 4% past it, the trade is short term on our trims with no adding, and a plain 4B that is still falling is much too soon to buy.

facts.quote: Stan Weinstein’s original strategy relied on weekly charts paired with the 30-week moving average which roughly correlates with the 150-day simple moving average.

facts.quote: During a Stage 4 Decline there is no reason to be long the stock

facts.claim: stageanalysis.net: buyers get in too early on a small base after a large decline, with price still under declining averages.

facts.quote: Stop first (by default a few cents under the day's low or the prior day's low, F62); the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
facts.claim: A3: stop first, a few cents under the day's low; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.quote: The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule (B20).
facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up, never wider; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.quote: Shares = account × risk % ÷ (entry − stop), rounded down, then capped: the size is the SMALLER of the risk-based size and the position cap
facts.claim: A5: shares are account times risk percent, divided by entry minus stop, rounded down, then capped.

facts.quote: Move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally. The first trim: the hard rule is a third at 3R; ideally anywhere from 3R to 6R, and in practice he mostly waits for 5R.
facts.claim: B19: breakeven between 2R and 5R; the hard rule for the first trim is a third at 3R.

facts.quote: A gap against the stop: the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. The low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.

facts.quote: With a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
facts.claim: B20's ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.

facts.quote: No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report; hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R.
facts.claim: B22: no new buys in the 3 days before a report; hold through one only if up 5R.

facts.quote: Trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.

facts.quote: No chasing: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.
facts.claim: C28: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

facts.quote: Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink (A5).

walkthroughs.title: NUS, April 2013: the longest base
steps: NUS, 2013. A December capitulation low, then a February higher low. Three months of flat 150 and 200-day lines.
A 19-day pause sits above a turning 50-day. The low is 48% under the high; the close is above the 200-day.
2013-04-18: price trades over the pause high. Buy at market, 49.99. Stop 49.05, 1.9% away.
Failure mode: Stage 4 resumes and the stop is hit. Instead the best run was 31.9R. Trim a third at 3R.

walkthroughs.title: PENN, November 2019: the picture-book shape
steps: PENN, 2019. A long Stage 4 under a falling 30-week line. The August low is 53% under the high.
An October higher low, 7.7% above it, then a 17-day pause above a 50-day that has turned up.
2019-11-05: price trades over the pause high, above the 200-day. Buy at market, 22.12. Stop 21.49, 2.8% away.
Failure mode: the break stalls under a falling long average, stop taken. Instead the best run was 15.7R. Trim at 3R.

walkthroughs.title: F, February 2024: the planned loss
steps: F, 2024. A 37.5% decline to 9.63, a higher low 3.6% above it, 70 sessions off the low.
A 12-day pause above the 50-day. The trigger day closes near its high.
2024-02-12: price trades over the pause high. Buy at market, 12.99. Stop 12.59, 3.1% away.
Failure mode: the next session fell to 12.48 and took the stop. Nothing in the setup was wrong; the loss was planned.

questions.q: In Weinstein's stage legend, what does a plain 4B mean?
choices: Late in the decline: too soon to buy
A bottom is in: buy now
questions.answer: Late in the decline: too soon to buy
questions.why: Late in the downtrend, and much too soon to consider buying. The buy is the 4B-, the one with the minus.
questions.lesson_line: A plain 4B is not a buy. Wait for the minus.

wrong.A bottom is in: buy now: That is the minus. A plain 4B is late in the downtrend and much too soon to consider buying.
wrong.Early in the decline: The B means late in the stage, not early.
wrong.A Stage 2 breakout: Stage 2 is the advance. A plain 4B is still the declining stage, and there is no reason to be long.

questions.q: What does the minus in 4B- say?
choices: The stock has seen its low for the cycle
The stock is still falling hard
The stock is already in Stage 2
questions.answer: The stock has seen its low for the cycle
questions.why: The stock has now seen its low for the cycle. It is not yet officially in Stage 1A, but the low is in.
questions.lesson_line: The minus says the low is in. Not yet a base, but the low is in.

wrong.The stock is still falling hard: That is a plain 4B. The minus says the low for the cycle is in.
wrong.The stock is already in Stage 2: It is not yet even officially in Stage 1A. The minus only says the low is in.
wrong.The stock is a short: The minus says the low for the cycle is in, so it is a long idea, not a short.

questions.q: A 4B- comes after a Stage 4 decline, with price under a falling 30-week line.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A Stage 4 decline comes first: at the low the 150-day, the 30-week line, was falling and price was under it.
questions.lesson_line: No decline first, no 4B-. The 30-week line was falling at the low.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The 30-week line is about the ___-day average.
questions.why: 150. The 30-week line roughly matches the 150-day average, and the 40-week line is the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Thirty weeks is about 150 days. Forty weeks is 200.

questions.q: A 4B- is a short-term trade on our trims, not a ride into Stage 2 with adds along the way.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. It is a short-term trade on the house trims: one price, one stop, no adding along the way.
questions.lesson_line: In and out on our trims. One price, one stop, no adds.

questions.q: A 4B- needs a close back above the 50-day average.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The close is above the 50-day, the recapture of the 50-day that Weinstein names.
questions.lesson_line: The 50-day has to be won back before the buy.

questions.q: We do not buy a 4B- while the close is still under the 200-day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, no long. Get back above it first.

questions.q: How is the cycle low found?
choices: Lowest low of the 252 sessions before
Lowest close of the last 20 sessions
The day with the most volume
questions.answer: Lowest low of the 252 sessions before
questions.why: The lowest low of the 252 sessions before the trigger. The 52-week high is the highest high of the 252 sessions before the cycle low.
questions.lesson_line: Find the cycle low first. Everything else is measured from it.

wrong.Lowest close of the last 20 sessions: That is a recent dip, not the low for the cycle. The cycle low looks back 252 sessions.
wrong.The 50-day average at its lowest: An average is not the low. The cycle low is the lowest low of the 252 sessions.
wrong.The day with the most volume: Volume does not pick the low. The lowest low of the 252 sessions does.

questions.q: How far above the cycle low should the higher low sit?
questions.answer: At least 3%
questions.why: At least 3%, set at least 10 sessions after the cycle low, after a rally of 5% or more.
questions.lesson_line: A higher low is a real step up, not a tie.

wrong.At least 15%: That asks for far too much. The line is 3%.
wrong.Any amount, even equal: An equal low is not higher. The higher low has to sit at least 3% above.
wrong.At least 1%: 1% is inside the noise. The line is 3%.

questions.q: How many closes above the 50-day make the minimum pause?
questions.why: 2 closes above the 50-day before the trigger. A pause of 5 to 20 sessions did best in our scan.
questions.lesson_line: Two closes above the 50-day is the minimum pause.

wrong.1: One close is a single day above the average, not a pause.
wrong.5: 5 sessions did well, but the minimum is 2.
wrong.10: 10 sessions is a longer pause. The minimum is 2.

questions.q: We take a 4B- only in a stock at $10 or more that trades $20 million a day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Price $10 or more and at least $20 million traded a day.
questions.lesson_line: A clean base in a thin stock is still a thin stock.

questions.q: What is the buy on a 4B-?
choices: Trades over the pause high, at market
A limit order at the higher low
questions.answer: Trades over the pause high, at market
questions.why: It trades over the highest high of the pause above the 50-day, during regular hours, bought at market.
questions.lesson_line: Over the pause high, in hours, at market.

wrong.The first close over the 50-day: The 50-day reclaim comes first. The buy waits for the pause and the trade over its high.
wrong.A limit order at the higher low: A limit at the higher low buys before the pause is built. Entries are market orders.
wrong.A close over the 200-day: Being over the 200-day is a gate, not the trigger. The trigger is the pause high.

questions.q: A buy 6 sessions after the cycle low is too early for a 4B-.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A 4B- needs at least 15 sessions from the cycle low to the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Give the base time. At least 15 sessions off the low.

questions.q: Bought at 22.12 with the stop at 21.49. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 24.01. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. This is PENN's buy.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: The 52-week high is 60.00 and the cycle low is 31.50. How far under the high is the low, in percent?
questions.why: 47.5%. The high minus the low, divided by the high.
questions.lesson_line: Depth is high minus low, over the high. Measure it.

questions.q: The cycle low is 20.00 and the higher low is 21.40. How far above the cycle low is it, in percent?
questions.why: 7%. The higher low over the cycle low, minus one. The higher low has to sit at least 3% above.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the step up from the cycle low.

questions.q: Volume on the down days into the higher low should dry up.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The down days of the higher-low pullback trade below the 50-day average volume.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet selling into the higher low is the picture.

questions.q: How much room do we want to the nearest overhead level?
questions.answer: At least 3R
questions.why: At least 3R from the entry to the nearest overhead level, counting only levels above the entry.
questions.lesson_line: Three R of room, or the trade is not worth it.

wrong.At least 1R: 1R does not reach the first trim at 3R. The room has to be 3R.
wrong.Any room at all: A wall just overhead is the named mistake. We want 3R.
wrong.At least 10R: 10R is far more than the first trim needs. The line is 3R.

questions.q: A fresh reason for the turn, like an earnings reaction, helps a 4B-.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True, as a cue, provided the buy is not in the 3 days before a report.
questions.lesson_line: A fresh reason helps. A report next week does not.

questions.q: After entry, the stop is the exit.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is the plan. It only moves up.

questions.q: Buy the open?
questions.story: The pause high is 40.00. The stock gaps open at 42.00.
choices: Buy at market; it is strong
questions.answer: Pass; 5% past the pause high
questions.why: Pass. Skip if already more than 4% above the trigger level; this is 5% over. Chasing costs size, because the stop stays put.
questions.lesson_line: More than 4% past the pause high is no trade.

wrong.Buy at market; it is strong: Past 4% the stop stays far away and the shares shrink. That is a chase.
wrong.Buy half size: Half of a chase is still a chase. The line is 4%.

questions.q: Buy it?
questions.story: A stock down 60% still makes new lows under a falling 30-week line. It looks cheap.
questions.answer: No; that is a plain 4B
questions.why: No. Never a 4B without the minus. A stock still making new lows is much too soon to consider buying.
questions.lesson_line: Cheap is not a reason. A falling stock is a falling stock.

wrong.Yes; it is cheap: Buying because it seems cheap is the named mistake.
wrong.Yes, a small starter: Size does not fix timing. It is much too soon to consider buying.

questions.q: What does that tell you?
questions.story: A stock bounces for three weeks, then closes under its cycle low.
choices: The low call was wrong; it is still a 4
A higher low; the setup is on
questions.answer: The low call was wrong; it is still a 4
questions.why: The low-for-the-cycle call was wrong. It is still a 4B or a 4.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the cycle low resets the count.

wrong.A bargain; buy more: A close under the cycle low is no bargain. The low was not the low.
wrong.A higher low; the setup is on: A higher low sits above the cycle low. This closed under it.

questions.q: Buy the break?
questions.story: A 4B- shape: a higher low, a 50-day reclaim and a pause. The close is still 12% under the 200-day.
questions.answer: No; no longs under the 200-day
questions.why: No. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. Wait until price is back above it.
questions.lesson_line: The shape is not enough. The 200-day comes first.

wrong.Yes; the shape is perfect: A perfect shape under the 200-day is still under the 200-day.
wrong.Yes, on half size: Half size does not change the 200-day rule.

questions.q: Bought at 12.37, stop 12.06. The stock trades to 13.92. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. That is where the second third comes off. This is AMD's buy.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 5R is the second trim.

questions.q: The stop moves to breakeven somewhere between 2R and 5R.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim.

questions.q: In our scan, which pause above the 50-day did worst?
questions.answer: A bare 2 to 4 session pause
questions.why: A bare 2 to 4 session pause: 15.7% reached 3R. The 5 to 10 session pause did best, at 25.9%.
questions.lesson_line: Give the pause a few days. A bare two-day pause did worst.

wrong.An 11 to 20 session pause: 23.1% reached 3R, well above the bare pause.
wrong.A 21 to 40 session pause: 21.3% reached 3R, also above the bare pause.

questions.q: Which group reading helps a 4B-?
choices: The group ETF closes above its 50-day
The group ETF falls the hardest
The group is not part of the call
questions.answer: The group ETF closes above its 50-day
questions.why: The stock's group ETF or index closing above its own 50-day. It helps most when the group is basing too and the stock is among the first to reclaim its 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: A turning group lifts a turning stock.

wrong.The group ETF falls the hardest: A weak group is the B- end. We want the group turning up too.
wrong.The group is not part of the call: A weak group is a named mistake. The group turning up helps.

questions.q: What does that do to the setup?
questions.story: A stock sets a higher low, then closes under it two weeks before the pause is done.
choices: It is off; the higher low failed
It is on; a fresh low is cheaper
Nothing; only the cycle low counts
questions.answer: It is off; the higher low failed
questions.why: It is off. A close under the higher low before the entry cancels the setup; the higher low did not hold.
questions.lesson_line: A higher low that breaks is not a higher low.

wrong.It is on; a fresh low is cheaper: A close under the higher low cancels the setup. A lower low is not a bargain.
wrong.Nothing; only the cycle low counts: A close under the cycle low also cancels it, but a close under the higher low does too.

questions.q: Is that a 4B-?
questions.story: A stock undercuts its low and reclaims it two sessions later. You want to buy the reclaim.
choices: No; a 4B- waits weeks for a higher low
questions.answer: No; a 4B- waits weeks for a higher low
questions.why: No. A 4B- never closes under its cycle low and waits 15 or more sessions for a higher low, a 50-day reclaim and a pause before the buy.
questions.lesson_line: An undercut and reclaim is quick. A 4B- takes weeks.

wrong.Yes; it reclaimed the low: That is a different setup that buys a quick reclaim. A 4B- never closes under its cycle low.
wrong.Yes, if volume is big: Volume does not make a quick reclaim into a 4B-. The 4B- waits for the base.

questions.q: Is that a 4B-?
questions.story: A stock flushes on twice its usual volume under every fast average. You buy the snap back two days later.
choices: Yes; it flushed to the low
Yes, if it holds the low
questions.answer: No; a capitulation snap back
questions.why: No. A capitulation buys the snap back within 3 sessions of a flush. A 4B- waits weeks for a higher low on drying volume and a 50-day reclaim.
questions.lesson_line: A snap back is quick. A 4B- takes weeks.

wrong.Yes; it flushed to the low: A flush buys the snap back. A 4B- waits for the base.
wrong.Yes, if it holds the low: Holding the low is not enough. A 4B- waits for a higher low and a 50-day reclaim.

questions.q: Is it a 4B- yet?
questions.story: A stock bottoms and rallies straight into its 50-day with no pullback.
choices: No; it has no higher low
questions.answer: No; it has no higher low
questions.why: No. A higher low is the critical signal, and a V straight up into the 50-day has not shown one.
questions.lesson_line: No pullback, no higher low, no 4B- yet.

wrong.Yes; it reclaimed the 50-day: The 50-day reclaim is one step. Without a higher low, it is a V.
wrong.Yes, on lower volume: Volume cannot stand in for a higher low.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: You would buy at 50.00 with the stop at 48.50. The falling 200-day sits at 52.00, just overhead.
questions.answer: Pass; only 1.33R of room
questions.why: Pass. We want at least 3R to the nearest overhead level, and the falling 200-day leaves only 1.33R.
questions.lesson_line: A wall just overhead is no trade. Count the room.

wrong.Take it; the 200-day will break: Buying right under a falling long average with less than 3R of room is the named mistake.
wrong.Take it, on half size: Half size does not buy more room.

questions.q: Buy the break?
questions.story: A clean pause break sets up for tomorrow. The company reports after the close in 2 days.
choices: No; no buys 3 sessions before a report
Yes, and sell before the report
questions.answer: No; no buys 3 sessions before a report
questions.why: No. No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report. Hold through a report only if up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Check the report date before every buy.

wrong.Yes; the shape is clean: A clean shape does not move the earnings window.
wrong.Yes, and sell before the report: The rule is no new buy in that window, not a quick trade through it.

questions.q: Buy the break?
questions.story: A pause breaks out, and the stock sits 12% over its 10-day average.
choices: Yes; it is a clean break
questions.answer: No; too stretched over the 10-day
questions.why: No. Skip if more than 10% above the 10-day average. This one is 12% over.
questions.lesson_line: A clean break, too far above its average, is a pass.

wrong.Yes; it is a clean break: The break is clean, but the stretch rule comes before the break.
wrong.Yes, on half size: Half size does not cure a stretch.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought a 4B- break 10 trading days ago. It sits at 0.7R, drifting under the falling 200-day.
choices: Hold; the stop has not traded
questions.answer: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing. The money has somewhere better to be.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not traded: The time stop is its own exit. Under 1R after 10 days, the money goes elsewhere.
wrong.Add; it is cheap: Adding along the way is the named mistake. One price, one stop.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A clean 4B- breaks the pause high, but the market reading just turned Red.
choices: No new long; the reading is Red
questions.answer: No new long; the reading is Red
questions.why: No new long. When the market reading turns Red there are no new longs, and existing trades keep their stops.
questions.lesson_line: A great base in a Red market still waits.

wrong.Buy; the base is great: Buying against the market is the named mistake. Red means no new longs.
wrong.Buy half size: Half size is still a new long in a Red market.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: A stock has reclaimed its 50-day and paused for a week. Today it closes back under the 50-day.
choices: Wait for a new 2-session pause above it
Buy the dip; it is cheaper
questions.answer: Wait for a new 2-session pause above it
questions.why: Wait for a new pause. A close back under the 50-day before the trigger re-arms the setup only after a new 2-session pause above it.
questions.lesson_line: Lost the 50-day, so wait for a fresh pause above it.

wrong.Buy the dip; it is cheaper: The setup is off until a new pause forms. A dip under the 50-day is no entry.
wrong.Move the stop to the 200-day: There is no position yet, and the 200-day is not the stop.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 1%. Buy 22.12, stop 21.49. How many shares?
questions.why: 793. Account times risk percent, divided by the buy minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 39.00, so 3R is 43.00. The next morning it opens at 43.60.
choices: Sell a third at the open
questions.answer: Sell a third at the open
questions.why: Sell a third at the open. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Take the trim the open hands you.

wrong.Wait for the close: The level is already passed. Waiting gives the gap time to fill.
wrong.Sell it all: A third at 3R. The rest waits for 5R and the trail.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 39.00. It gaps open at 38.20, and the first 30-minute low is 37.80.
questions.answer: Out; the loss is past 2R
questions.why: Out. On a gap through the stop the first 30-minute low is the new stop, but past 2R you get out. A low of 37.80 is more than 2R from 40.00.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop has a ceiling of 2R.

wrong.The new stop is 37.80: The 30-minute low is the stop only while the loss is inside 2R. This one is past it.
wrong.Hold; gaps fill: Hope is not a rule. The gap rule has a ceiling, and this is past it.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You hold the last third of a fast mover after both trims. Today it closes under its 10-day.
choices: Sell the last third on that close
questions.answer: Sell the last third on that close
questions.why: Sell the last third. A fast mover trails the 10-day, and we sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: The trail is a close under the 10-day. Sell it.

wrong.Hold until the 50-day breaks: The trail is the 10-day for a fast mover, not the 50-day.
wrong.Move the stop down: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.

questions.q: What do you tell them?
questions.story: Your 4B- trade is working. A friend says to add along the way, as some traders do.
choices: No; one price, one stop, no adding
Yes; add on each higher low
questions.answer: No; one price, one stop, no adding
questions.why: No. Size from the stop; one price, one stop, no adding along the way. Adding on the way up is the named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Full size once. A winner is not a reason to add.

wrong.Yes; add on each higher low: Adding to it on the way up is the named mistake.
wrong.Yes, but only half size: A smaller add is still an add with a second price and a second stop.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You are up 4R in four days on a vertical, wide-range burst.
choices: Sell a big part into the burst
Hold it all; the trail will handle it
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the burst
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. A climax run on your own long is a judgment call, and selling a big part is the rule.
questions.lesson_line: A vertical burst is for selling into.

wrong.Add; it is going parabolic: Adding is the named mistake, and a burst is for selling into.
wrong.Hold it all; the trail will handle it: The trail catches the turn late. A burst is the moment to bank a big part.

questions.q: Our position should be at most 1% of the stock's average daily volume.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: Size to the stock's volume, not just the stop.

questions.q: How does the market change the buy?
questions.story: After a broad market decline the index turns up. A stock is among the first in its group to reclaim its 50-day.
choices: Good; start with a few positions
Wait; the market must make a new high
Go all in on this one
questions.answer: Good; start with a few positions
questions.why: Good conditions. The best turns come once the market itself turns up, and after a correction you start with a few positions and add more only as they work.
questions.lesson_line: A market turning up is the wind behind the turn.

wrong.Wait; the market must make a new high: The best turns come when the market itself turns back up, not after a new high.
wrong.Go all in on this one: After a correction, start with a few positions and add more only as the first ones work.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: Your 4B- stalls under the falling 200-day and slides toward the old low. A friend says to hold it as an investment.
choices: Sell by the rules; never hold Stage 4
Hold it; it is a long-term bottom
Add to it; it is cheaper
questions.answer: Sell by the rules; never hold Stage 4
questions.why: Sell by the rules. A 4B- is a short-term trade, and treating it as an investment and holding it back into Stage 4 is the named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Do not turn a short-term trade into an investment.

wrong.Hold it; it is a long-term bottom: Holding a short-term trade back down into Stage 4 is the named mistake.
wrong.Add to it; it is cheaper: Adding is the named mistake, and the stop is the exit.

questions.q: The stop traded. Did the rules fail?
questions.story: You bought a 4B- at 12.99 with the stop at 12.59. A 37.5% decline, a higher low, a 12-day pause. The next session fell to 12.48.
choices: No; a planned loss, rules followed
Yes; the stop was too tight
questions.answer: No; a planned loss, rules followed
questions.why: No. This was a correct 4B- that lost. The stop is the plan, and the loss was planned.
questions.lesson_line: A correct setup can lose. The stop makes it small.

wrong.Yes; the stop was too tight: The stop sits where the rules put it. Widening it to dodge a loss is the mistake.
wrong.Yes; we bought too late: The break was inside the 4% chase cap and everything passed.

questions.q: After the first stop-out, when do you buy again?
questions.story: A 39% drop to the March 2020 low, a higher low, a 13-day pause. The break closed mid-range and the next day took the 1.4% stop.
choices: Only on a new trigger after a new pause
At once; it is the same setup
questions.answer: Only on a new trigger after a new pause
questions.why: Only on a new trigger. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade, and it re-arms only after a new 2-session pause above the 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: A V bottom can fail twice. Re-arm on a new pause.

wrong.At once; it is the same setup: After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade.
wrong.Never again on this stock: The setup can re-arm. The real move came from a third base.

questions.q: What grade cue flagged this one?
questions.story: MSFT, 2001: a 66% Stage 4 decline, a 92-session base, an 18-day pause. The break reached a fraction of 1R, then the stop.
questions.answer: A falling 200-day over the trade
questions.why: A falling 200-day over the trade. The long averages should be flat or turning, not still falling steeply.
questions.lesson_line: Watch the long averages. A falling 200-day is overhead supply.

wrong.The pause was too long: An 18-day pause is inside the 5 to 20 sessions that did best.
wrong.The base was too short: A 92-session base is long. The falling long average was the cue.

questions.q: Which check could have kept you out?
questions.story: Two 4B- triggers in a bear market, months apart. Each looked clean, and each stopped the next session.
questions.answer: The market reading
questions.why: The market reading. Two 4B- triggers in the 2008 bear were both stopped without trading above the entry. Buying against the market is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Forest first, then the trees. Check the market.

wrong.A tighter stop: A tighter stop would have been hit even sooner. The missing filter was the market.
wrong.A bigger position: More size on a losing setup only loses more.

questions.q: Is it a 4B-?
questions.story: A stock drops 34% from its high. At the cycle low the 150-day was rising: 528.74 against 521.41 twenty sessions earlier.
choices: No; a pullback in an uptrend
Yes; the drop is deep enough
questions.answer: No; a pullback in an uptrend
questions.why: No. A 34% drop under a 150-day that was still rising at the low is a pullback in an uptrend, a Remount or a pullback buy, not a Stage 4 turn.
questions.lesson_line: Read the 150-day at the low before you name it.

wrong.Yes; the drop is deep enough: A deep drop is not a Stage 4. The 150-day was rising at the low.
wrong.Yes, if volume dried up: Dry volume does not change a rising 150-day at the low.

questions.q: Is that a real higher low?
questions.story: A V off the January 2019 low. The higher low sits 6.8% above the cycle low, but the high off the low was only 4.1% above it.
choices: No; no 5% rally before it, so one leg
Yes; it is above the cycle low
questions.answer: No; no 5% rally before it, so one leg
questions.why: No. The higher low sits 6.8% above the cycle low, but no 5% rally came before it, so it is one leg, not a base.
questions.lesson_line: A higher low needs a rally before it. Otherwise it is one leg.

wrong.Yes; it is above the cycle low: Above the cycle low is not enough. A rally of 5% or more has to come before it.
wrong.Yes, if volume dried up: Dry volume does not make one leg into a base.

questions.q: Does our earnings rule allow that buy?
questions.story: A vendor's example buys a 50-day reclaim at 189 on 2022-07-15 or 2022-07-18. The company reports after the close on 2022-07-19.
choices: No; within 3 sessions of the report
questions.answer: No; within 3 sessions of the report
questions.why: No. No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report. The 50-day reclaim was bought one to two sessions before the report, and most of the move was the earnings gap.
questions.lesson_line: Check the report date, even on a famous chart.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim was clean: A clean reclaim does not move the earnings window.
wrong.Yes, if it holds the 50-day: Holding the 50-day does not change the report date.

questions.q: Write the plan.
questions.story: NUS, April 2013: 78 sessions off a December low, a February higher low, and a 19-day pause above a turning 50-day.
choices: Wait for a Stage 2 breakout instead
questions.answer: Buy 49.99, stop 49.05, a third at 3R
questions.why: Buy at market, 49.99, once price trades over the pause high. Stop 49.05, 1.9% away. A third comes off at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open.

wrong.Buy 49.99, stop 45.00, hold it all: The stop here sat 1.9% away; 45.00 is far wider. And a third comes off at 3R.
wrong.Wait for a Stage 2 breakout instead: That is a different trade. This is the 4B-, the short-term play.

questions.q: Which gets the bigger size?
questions.story: Two 4B- breaks. A: a clean higher low, a tight pause on a flat 50-day, the group and market turning up. B: no higher low, a steeply falling 50-day, the falling 200-day just overhead.
questions.answer: A; every cue lines up
questions.why: A. A clean higher low on light volume, a tight pause on a flat 50-day, and a group and market turning up are the A+ end. No higher low, a falling 50-day and a falling 200-day overhead are the B- end.
questions.lesson_line: Same setup, different grade. The base and the backdrop set the size.

wrong.B; it has more upside: B has a wall overhead and no higher low. Its room is the problem.
wrong.Equal; both broke out: Both broke the pause high, but the base and the backdrop differ.

questions.q: Did the system break?
questions.story: You take five 4B- trades by the rules. Four stop out, and one runs for 5R.
choices: No; about one in five reaches 3R
Yes; the setup does not work
questions.answer: No; about one in five reaches 3R
questions.why: No. Above the 200-day, 22.2% of the scan's 4B- hits reached 3R, so four stops in five tries is ordinary. The trims and the trail pay for the losses.
questions.lesson_line: A 4B- loses often. Small stops and trims keep it alive.

wrong.Yes; the setup does not work: A low hit rate with small stops and trims is the design, not a failure.
wrong.Yes; widen the stops: Widening the stop is the mistake. A fixed small stop is what keeps the losses small.

questions.q: In Bulkowski's own trades, Stage 4 buys made money about 24% of the time.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Bulkowski's own Stage 4 buys made money 24% of the time, so a 4B- is a low-hit-rate trade that lives on small stops and trims.
questions.lesson_line: Buying near a Stage 4 low is a low-odds trade. Trade it small and short.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. A washout, a higher low, a pause over the 50-day. Above its 200-day? Take it or pass.
choices: Take it; above the 200-day, higher low
Pass; there is no higher low
questions.answer: Take it; above the 200-day, higher low
